Let AK be the ring of adeles of K, and for any set S, let C(S) denote the adelic closure of S. Then   C Y ∩ Of (P ) = Y (AK ) ∩ C Of (P ).

refined_question: Is the following Dynamical Brauer-Manin conjecture true? Let K be a number field, let X/K be a variety, let f : X -> X be a morphism defined over K, let Y subset X be a subvariety defined over K, and let P be a point of X(K). Write O_f(P) = {f^n(P) : n >= 0}. View X(K) diagonally inside X(A_K), where A_K is the adele ring of K, and for any subset S of X(A_K) let C(S) denote its closure in the adelic topology. Must one have C(Y ∩ O_f(P)) = Y(A_K) ∩ C(O_f(P))?
justification: The draft matches the statement printed in §22 as Conjecture 22.3 almost verbatim; the main repair needed is to restore the left-hand side as the adelic closure of Y ∩ O_f(P). The surrounding paragraph in §22 identifies this as a local-global problem related to the Dynamical Mordell-Lang Conjecture and glosses it as saying that adelic or p-adic data attached to the orbit should determine the orbit. The notation O_f(P) is defined earlier in §2, and Conjecture 7.1 in §7 supplies the Dynamical Mordell-Lang context explicitly referenced just before Conjecture 22.3. Because this paper is a survey and the draft clearly points to the local-global section, Conjecture 22.3 is the nearest official formulation in the paper.
